concepts.def: Sequence of growth, DNA replication, and division that all body cells go through.
Long DNA molecule wound around proteins; visible during cell division.
Before division, each chromosome makes an exact copy of itself.
Cell division producing two genetically identical daughter cells; used for growth and repair.
A cell produced by cell division.
Embryonic stem cells can become any cell type; adult stem cells (e.g. bone marrow) are more limited.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Cell Division & Genetics — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Cell Division & Genetics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Cell Division & Genetics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
